name: Mendel's Peas
description: Phenotype counts from Mendel's dihybrid pea cross (n=556) vs. the 9:3:3:1 genetic ratio. IMS Ch. 16 (goodness-of-fit).
studyDescription: Gregor Mendel classified 556 pea plants from a dihybrid cross by seed shape (round/wrinkled) and color (yellow/green). Mendel's theory of independent assortment predicts the four phenotypes in a 9:3:3:1 ratio. The goodness-of-fit test asks whether the observed counts are consistent with that predicted ratio.

variableDescriptions.phenotype: The seed's combined shape-and-color phenotype: Round Yellow, Round Green, Wrinkled Yellow, or Wrinkled Green.

sourceDetail: Mendel, G. (1866), "Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden." The classic dihybrid cross. χ² = 0.47, df = 3, p ≈ 0.925 — a famously close fit to the 9:3:3:1 ratio.
